content.text:
The spec and code still support it, though. The ContainerEnvironmentScope, ProjectDataScope (`runCodeTasksInContainer`), HarnessIntegrationScope and Sending all describe the "Run code tasks in a container" option. `src/container.rs` has a `RunKind::Code` plan with the cache volume, and the Settings window has the toggle. It's off by default, so it's easy to never notice.

Here's the prompt with that removed as well:

---

> Code tasks never run in a container, and a project's harness sessions from containerized runs are kept in the project, so a conversation carries on across runs, restarts, and moves of the project.
>
> **Remove code containerization:** Spec tasks, a Chain prompt's spec steps and spec follow-up, and questions from the Ask tab are the only runs in a container. Code tasks and a Chain prompt's code step always run on the host, with their protected locations, as the HarnessIntegrationScope says. Remove the project's "Run code tasks in a container" option everywhere: the `runCodeTasksInContainer` setting from `.suspense/settings.json` in the ProjectDataScope, its toggle from the SettingsWindowScope, the Code section of the ContainerEnvironmentScope's Mounts, the project's caches and their volume, and every "while the project's option is on" in the ContainerEnvironmentScope, the HarnessIntegrationScope, the PromptModeScope, and Sending, including the rule that turning the option on or off starts the code lane on a new conversation. Where `.suspense/settings.json` then holds nothing, the ProjectDataScope says so, or drops it if nothing else uses it. A Code task never needs Podman.
>
> **ContainerEnvironmentScope, Volumes:** the harness's sessions are no longer kept in Podman volumes. They are kept in the project, in `.suspense/sessions/`, one folder per conversation: `spec` for the spec lane and `questions` for the Ask tab's questions. Each run mounts only its own conversation's folder, read and write, where the harness keeps its sessions under its home, never `.suspense/sessions/` as a whole, so no run sees another conversation's sessions. The application creates the folder before the run if it isn't there. The only volumes left are one per harness, for its login and settings, shared by every project, as now. Losing the project's sessions folder costs only the conversations' context: the next run starts a new conversation, as when a session can't be resumed. Sessions kept in volumes before this aren't carried over; each conversation starts fresh.
>
> **ContainerEnvironmentScope, Mounts and Paths:** the project is mounted at the same fixed path in the container, `/workspace`, on every platform, and the run works there, so a harness that keys its sessions on its working directory, as Claude Code does, finds them again after the project moves. Change Mounts so it no longer says each location is mounted at its host path where the platform allows. Paths now applies on every platform: every path a run reports is mapped back to its host path before it is shown or opened. Only a path that is `/workspace` or begins with `/workspace/` is mapped, never text that merely contains it, as `/workspace-old`. A path that maps to nothing on the host is shown as the run gave it, and opens nothing, as now.
>
> **ProjectDataScope:** add `.suspense/sessions/` to the project data. It belongs to this machine: git ignores it and it is never committed, since it holds the harness's transcripts. Change the paragraph that says the harnesses' sessions aren't in `.suspense`: the images and logins still aren't, but the sessions now are.
>
> **HarnessIntegrationScope:** the spec lane and the questions always run in a container and the code lane always on the host, so each conversation is only ever carried on where it began. A spec lane or questions conversation from before this, whose session the project's sessions folder doesn't hold, is tried, and if the harness has no such session, it is sent again at once as a new conversation, as now.

---

The changes from the last draft:
- **Project ID dropped.** Its only job was naming the cache volume.
- **The saved container/host flag dropped.** Each lane now always runs in the same place, so a conversation can only ever be resumed where it began.
